limitations: Availability describes documented member groups and browser declarations. Compilation tests do not prove rendering, timing or complete behavioral parity.
Shaders are fragment shaders; the browser runs them with WebGL.

File access and recorder APIs are desktop-only; Pixels reads the stage on the graphics card. Tiled reads finite orthogonal TMX/TSX maps from workspace files or URLs. SaveData instead persists plain game data in IndexedDB, scoped to the hosting origin and browser profile.
Reference examples are compiled with the standard flavor. Existing NRW runtime fixtures and a separate declaration inventory cover the NRW flavor.
Java compiler dialect differences also apply, including Java package access and unsupported standard-library methods.

Window/useFullScreen.reason: The embedded browser output uses its enclosing page; this desktop window option only reports a limitation.

Window/useSplashLogo.reason: The browser has no desktop splash window. This option only reports a limitation.

Window/use.reason: Extensions load through the desktop's ServiceLoader and run against its window and render threads. The browser ships its extensions natively; it does not load external or custom extensions.

Sprite/extension.reason: For extensions, which run against the desktop's window and render threads. The browser ships its extensions natively and loads no others.

Stage/extension.reason: For extensions, which run against the desktop's window and render threads. The browser ships its extensions natively and loads no others.
